Snt ma’am teaches very well. If you are planning to major in Finance, she is one of the best choices. The reason is that she delivers the entire lecture in Bangla, which makes it easier to understand many finance-related terms. But she is very fast-going. Each class lasts only about 35–40 minutes.
Now let’s talk about the question pattern. There are 5 quizzes (best 3 are counted), 2 midterms, a final exam, a report submission, and performance marks. The quizzes include MCQs and short math problems, which can be handled if you study the slides properly. The real challenge is the midterms and final. The questions there are hard—you could call them purely conceptual. She marks a lot of math problems, and you must solve them. Alongside that, your basics in finance and critical thinking must be extremely strong; otherwise, you’ll struggle a lot in exams.
Another thing—she is very strict with exam marking. For example, suppose there’s a math problem worth 7 marks, divided into two parts. You write the formula correctly, solve the first part accurately, but make a mistake in the second part. Many faculty members would give partial marks for the correct part. But Snt ma’am won’t give any partial marks. You’ll get zero for that entire problem. So, you have to study hard if you want a good grade in Finance under her. She will give you a tough time. If you can handle it, then good. If not, the entire semester might turn into a nightmare.
Now about the report. She doesn’t make it too difficult there—just follow the outline. The reason I mentioned “performance” separately is because, at the end of each chapter, she marks 5–10 math problems from the book. You have to solve them and write them down in your notebook. Later, if she calls you to solve a problem on the board, you’ll have to solve it there. If you succeed, you’ll get performance marks. But if she never calls you and you never solve a problem on the board, then you’ll get 0 out of 5 in performance.
Her grading is fair. She doesn’t curve for everyone—only for those she feels put in the effort.
So, the final word is this: if you want to endure a lot of struggle in Fin254 and come out with a good grade, she’s the best. But if you think you’re not good at math and want to complete the course easily, then I would suggest changing your faculty.
